name: Cortagen
lead: Cortagen is a synthetic tetrapeptide with the sequence Ala-Glu-Asp-Pro, made by Vladimir Khavinson's group in Russia from the amino-acid analysis of Cortexin, a natural brain-cortex peptide preparation [1]. It is one of the short synthetic peptide bioregulators the group proposes as tissue-specific regulators of ageing-related changes [1].

Published work consists of cell-culture, animal and small biochemical studies, many from the developers' laboratory. They examined gene expression in mouse heart [1], interleukin-2 expression [2][4], sciatic nerve regeneration [5] and free-radical processes [7]. One Russian report compared Cortexin and Cortagen in brain function in chronic ischaemia [10].
It is not an appearance product and no published trial in healthy people examines it.

paras: A microarray study in mice reported that Cortagen altered gene expression in heart tissue, which the authors framed as part of screening molecular targets of peptide bioregulators in ageing [1]. In rat and mouse cell systems, Cortagen had weaker immunomodulating effects than the related peptides Vilon and Epithalon: it produced no comitogenic effect on thymocytes [3] and a less pronounced effect on interleukin-2 mRNA in splenocytes [4], although in vivo work reported modulation of interleukin-2 expression in hypothalamic cells [2].

Other reports examined its effect on sciatic nerve regeneration [5], tissue-specific effects of peptides [6], free-radical processes [7], and lymphocyte chromatin and epigenetic markers in old cells [8][9]. A Russian paper compared Cortexin and Cortagen in functional and metabolic brain disorders in chronic ischaemia [10].
No studies found. The existing literature is limited to cell-culture, animal and chromatin work, plus one Russian-language report on brain ischaemia [10].

card.summary: Khavinson brain-derived tetrapeptide (AEDP) studied only in cells and animals; no appearance evidence.
card.note: Research is mostly from the developers' laboratory; not an appearance product.

quick.overview:
Cortagen is a four-amino-acid peptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Pro) made by Vladimir Khavinson's Russian group, modelled on a brain-cortex peptide extract called Cortexin.

Studies are limited to cells, rodents and a few small reports. No human trial for appearance exists.
quick.mechanism: Its developers propose that short peptides regulate gene expression in a tissue-specific way. Studies report changes in gene and interleukin-2 expression in cell and animal models.
quick.risks: Human safety data are essentially absent from the published literature, and it is not an approved drug in Western countries.
